diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is a closed subspace of $\mathcal{L}_1(\mu)$ for some measure $\mu$
which means the embedding $id:E\rightarrow F$ is a compact embedding
By Theorem \ref{theorem:Lpembed}, $\hat{E}$ is isometric to a subspace of $L_{s'}(\mu)$

issues.failure_explanation: Being an RKBS does not make E a closed subspace of F. If an infinite-dimensional E were closed in F, the open mapping theorem would make the E- and F-norms equivalent on E, and a compact identity would then force E to be finite-dimensional. So \hat E is not even complete. A continuous injection of l_inf into L_1 does not make \hat E, which carries the sup norm, a closed subspace of L_1. Elements of l_inf(X) need not be measurable either. Theorem Lpembed is therefore used outside its hypotheses. Even when it applies, it gives an isomorphic embedding, not the claimed isometric one.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis controls only vectors with ||x||_E<=1, but the proof applies it to rescaled vectors known only to satisfy ||x||_F<=1. The final normalization by max||x_i||_E cannot produce a bound in terms of ||x_i||_F. Counterexample: take E = {x : sum 2^k|x_k| < inf} and F = l_inf(N). Then E[||sum eps_i x_i||_inf] <= sum_k sqrt(n) 2^{-k} <= 2 sqrt(n), so the hypothesis holds with p'=2. Yet the finitely supported vectors x_i(eta)=eta_i on {+-1}^n give ||sum eps_i x_i||_inf = n, so \hat E has no type s'>1.
